tldr: A prespecified vector of marginal quantile treatment effects requires allocation for its whole simultaneous rectangle. For any fixed positive coordinate weights, the exact confidence-indexed minimum Gaussian radius under complementary arm probabilities and unknown population stratum weights is characterized by the complete truncated-Gaussian sensitivity matrix and certified globally by a supporting-gradient enclosure. A legal two-quantile exhibit has a certified 95-percent oracle radius between 2.557414 and 2.557416, strictly below the maximum-variance design radius; for every compact confidence range inside \((0,1/2)\), one relatively open legal coefficient neighborhood preserves the separation, and two finite confidence levels retain distinct optimizers. Pooled adaptive quantile inversion and a predictable plug-in learner attain the oracle radius and simultaneous coverage at covariance-learning rate \(O_P((\log n/n)^{1/4})\). Scalar adaptive QTE efficiency is credited to Li et al.; the proved contribution couples vector allocation, global certification and calibrated attainment.
gap: Jiang et al. give adjusted QTE process inference at a given allocation. Li et al., Section 2 and Theorems 1--2, derive the scalar optimal allocation and attain its variance adaptively. This is a different objective; no scalar efficiency or weaker-condition advance over Li is claimed.
